accessNotes: The three public plan pages exposed six USD-denominated account sizes with EUR list prices and lower Summer Promo prices. Only the struck-through EUR list prices are captured; SUMMER30, SUMMER25 and SUMMER15 prices are deliberately excluded because they are temporary promotions. BrightFunded's help-center restricted-country article lists Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Vietnam and Pakistan, while its Terms and Conditions list only the first five; this first-party conflict is unresolved. India appears in neither list as captured on 2026-08-10, but that is an availability observation rather than legal or regulatory approval. The reward-split article says the first request is after 30 days and subsequent requests every 14 days, but its add-on list also labels bi-weekly payouts as an add-on; the captured first-payout value remains the unambiguous 30-day default and the wording conflict is retained in notes.

fieldEvidence.phases: The plan is titled '1-Step Challenge' and the current-rules table has only a Phase 1 target for 1-Step.
fieldEvidence.profitTargets.phase1: The plan card says 'Profit Target 10% Phase 1'; the current-rules table also lists 1-Step Phase 1 at 10%.
fieldEvidence.dailyLossPct: Current-rules table: '1-Step | 3%' daily drawdown; the plan card also says 'Max. Daily Loss 3%'.
fieldEvidence.maxLossPct: Current-rules table: '1-Step | 6% | Trailing'; the plan card also says 'Max. Total Loss 6%'.
fieldEvidence.drawdownType: The current-rules article says trailing drawdown follows the highest equity and locks at the original balance after equity grows 6% above the initial balance.
fieldEvidence.minTradingDays: Current-rules table: '1-Step | 5'; the plan cards say 'Min. Trading Days 5 Days'.
fieldEvidence.maxTradingDays: The plan page says 'Unlimited Trading Period' and the Terms say the Challenge lasts for unlimited days; null represents no finite maximum.
fieldEvidence.consistencyRulePct: The plan page says 'No Consistency Rules' and 'No rules on how you size, time, or distribute your trades'; null is retained because no percentage cap exists.
fieldEvidence.profitSplitPct: The reward-split article says 'The Profit Split is 80/20 by default'; 90% requires an add-on and 100% requires scaling.
fieldEvidence.payoutFirstDays: The reward-split article says the first Reward Split can be requested 30 days after the first funded trade.
fieldEvidence.payoutFrequency: The reward-split article says subsequent Reward Splits can be requested bi-weekly (14 days).
fieldEvidence.rules.news: Evaluation phases allow unrestricted news trading, but funded accounts prohibit execution during the 5 minutes before and after high-impact news; therefore restricted.
fieldEvidence.rules.weekend: The weekend-holding article says traders may hold positions over the weekend.
fieldEvidence.rules.overnight: The overnight-holding article says positions do not need to be closed overnight.
fieldEvidence.rules.ea: The EA article says EAs are permitted but API and automated trading are not supported on DXtrade; therefore restricted across the product's platform choices.
fieldEvidence.rules.copyTrading: The copy-trading article permits copying only among accounts owned by the same individual and prohibits third-party and signal copying; therefore restricted.
fieldEvidence.refundable: The refund article allows a refund within 30 days only before any trade is made.

notes: All fees are EUR list prices. Temporary SUMMER30 pricing is deliberately excluded.
The 6% maximum drawdown trails the highest equity in real time and locks at the original balance after the account reaches 6% growth.
The base funded reward split is 80%; 90% is a paid add-on and 100% is available only through scaling.

The first standard payout window is 30 days after the first funded trade, then 14 days. The help article also calls bi-weekly payouts an add-on, creating an unresolved wording conflict; weekly or earlier cycles are paid add-ons.
News trading is unrestricted in evaluation but has a 10-minute execution restriction on funded accounts.

The separately advertised 100% challenge-fee refund is a checkout add-on, not included in the captured list price. The refundable tier flag instead records the standard unused-account refund within 30 days.
